title: FOMC communications blackout begins (through 2027-10-28) — it opens ten days after the September minutes close the Committee's last unrestricted word
source: EST: THE BOARD'S OWN POLICY TEXT, DECODED FROM THE PRIMARY PDF BY THIS SESSION rather than inherited. federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/files/fomc-blackout-period-calendar.pdf fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 98,013 bytes); its 60 content streams were inflated in-session and its footnote reads verbatim, on a document titled "2025-2027 FOMC Trading and External Communications Blackout Calendar": "The blackout period will begin at 12:00 a.m. Eastern Time the second Saturday before a meeting and end at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time the day after a meeting. For example, if the Committee meeting starts on a Tuesday, the blackout period will begin at the start of the Saturday that falls ten days earlier, and if the meeting ends on a Wednesday, the blackout period will end at the end of Thursday." THE MEETING is federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm's 2027 panel, also fetched direct this session (HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes, stamp "Last Update: August 19, 2026"), reading verbatim "October 26-27" with no SEP asterisk. Applying the rule: 2027-10-26 is a TUESDAY, ten days earlier is SATURDAY 2027-10-16, and the meeting ends Wednesday 2027-10-27 so the window closes at the end of Thursday 2027-10-28. WHAT THIS SESSION DID NOT DO, STATED PLAINLY: it did not re-decode the PDF's shaded calendar cells -- the shading lives in graphics operators, not in the text layer this session inflated. It does not need to. This repo's fomc-blackout-start-2027-04-17 entry already records the decoded 2027 windows verbatim as "Jan 16-28, Mar 6-18, Apr 17-29, May 29 -> Jun 10, Jul 17-29, Sep 4-16, OCT 16-28, Nov 27 -> Dec 9", and the rule derived independently here reproduces that October window TO THE DAY, as it also reproduces all four other 2027 blackout entries this calendar already carries (01-16, 03-06, 04-17, 05-29, 09-04). Filed estimate because a firm rule applied to a date the Board itself calls tentative cannot outrank its input -- the same page states "Each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it" -- so the promotion trigger is the 2027-09-14/15 meeting ratifying October 26-27. Discovered during the fomc-minutes-2027-10-06 initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: PROPOSED by the fomc-minutes-2027-10-06 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). THE HOLE IS THE SAME SHAPE AS ITS SIBLING PROPOSAL'S: this calendar tracks fomc-blackout-start entries for 2026-09-05, 2026-10-17, 2026-11-28, 2027-01-16, 2027-03-06, 2027-04-17, 2027-05-29 and 2027-09-04, plus a proposal for 2027-07-17 -- an unbroken series that simply stops after September 2027, leaving the October window untracked even though the repo's own decode already names it. IMPACT medium matches every other entry in the blackout series. WHY IT MATTERS TO THE PARENT, AND THE ONE THING NOT TO CONCLUDE FROM IT: the 2027-10-06 minutes land TEN DAYS BEFORE this gate opens, so they are comfortably outside it -- and they are effectively the Committee's last unrestricted communication before the October decision, since the only scheduled Fed speech window between them is 2027-10-07 to 2027-10-15. That is a fact about the communications calendar, NOT a signal: the parent ledger measured minutes days against 4,950 sessions and found the index ordinary (157 releases, 0.747% mean absolute move against a 0.797% baseline) and every apparent implied-vol edge dissolving under a placebo control, so nothing about this adjacency licenses an entry. THE DISPLACEMENT RISK IS THE ONE TO CARRY FORWARD: if the 2027-09-14/15 meeting ratifies an October meeting other than 26-27, this date moves with it and so does the parent's release date -- the two proposals filed by this lane die together with the meeting they are both derived from. Proposed as an estimate; estimate widens caution only.
